answer: Seats are sold by tide. Once per tide a block opens and the k-th seat costs 2^k times the base, burned, so a farm crowding one tide pays exponentially while newcomers take early cheap seats. Each seat needs shale behind it, a layered bond slashed if its answers grade as junk, and a seat may be inherited through a thread only once per identity, fee doubling so shells cannot be passed down. Unused seats lapse at tide end, killing stockpiling; splitting across tides looks cheaper, yet an old seat carries no depth until its thread is re-audited, which costs a cluster far more than one fresh seat.
